title: Lebanese cabinet orders army to draw up plan to disarm Hezbollah
body:
On 5 August 2025 Lebanon's cabinet, chaired by President Joseph Aoun, tasked the Lebanese army with drawing up a plan to disarm Hezbollah. Prime Minister Nawaf Salam announced the decision, which Al-Monitor called unprecedented because other civil war factions gave up their weapons decades ago. The plan was to be in place before the end of 2025 and presented to the cabinet by the end of August for discussion and approval.

The decision followed heavy US pressure and formed part of implementing the November 2024 ceasefire that ended more than a year of hostilities with Israel. The cabinet was to keep discussing a proposal from US envoy Tom Barrack that included a disarmament timetable. Barrack had urged Lebanon to act to impose a state monopoly on weapons.

Hezbollah chief Naim Qassem said the group would not disarm while Israeli attacks continued and rejected any timetable imposed under Israeli aggression. He also demanded reconstruction, an end to Israeli attacks, Israeli withdrawal from five border areas and the release of prisoners, and called the US plan dictates rather than an agreement. Health Minister Rakan Nassereldine, who is affiliated with Hezbollah, and Environment Minister Tamara Elzein, who is affiliated with Amal, walked out of the session in disagreement with the decision.
